summary.text: 课 means “lesson,” “course,” or “classwork” and is the standardized simplified form of 課. The traditional graph is analyzed as a speech-related category plus a sound component; its older gloss “test or examine” has no established link to the school meanings.

formation.text: 课 is derived from traditional 課 through standardized simplification. The traditional graph 課 is phonosemantic: 言 contributes a speech-related meaning category, and 果 is identified as the sound component. The simplified 讠 is the standardized counterpart of 言 here; the traditional semantic analysis is scoped to 課.

components.text: 讠 is the standardized simplified counterpart of 言 within traditional 課. The historical analysis assigns the speech-related category role to 言; the modern standard documents the graphic mapping, not a separate ancient role for 讠.
In traditional 課, 言 contributes the speech-related meaning category. No earlier graphic form for this component in 課 is established here.
果 is identified as the phonetic component in 課 and remains visible in simplified 课.

sound_limitation.text: A same-system ancient reading comparison for 果 and 課 is unavailable in the supplied Baxter–Sagart data; the modern Mandarin pair does not establish their historical sound relation.

sound.text: In Modern Mandarin, 果 is guǒ and 課 is kè. This current pair does not prove the historical sound relation.

history.text: The traditional graph 課 is analyzed as 从言、果聲 and glossed 試也, “test or examine.” This historical dictionary account does not establish the graph’s earliest form or date of appearance.
The standardized simplified form 课 corresponds to 課: 果 remains, while 言 is represented by 讠. The orthographic relationship is supported, but its adoption date is not established.

uncertainties.text: The earliest attestation and dated graphic history of 課 remain unresolved; no corruption account is supported by the inspected evidence.
The traditional analysis identifies 果 as the phonetic component, but the available reconstruction data provides no same-system ancient comparison for 果 and 課.
The simplified counterpart is documented, but its adoption date is not established.

senses.text: A traditional dictionary glosses 課 as “test” or “examine.” This does not establish that meaning as the graph’s original meaning or earliest use.
A reported Former Han citation uses 課 in the context of assessing officials; its textual dating details were not fully verified.
A traditional dictionary presents “order or rank” as an extension from testing or examination, without dating the development.
A traditional dictionary presents taxation as an extension from testing or examination, without dating the development.
Current definitions include lesson, course, and classwork. Their historical connection, if any, to testing or official assessment is unclear.
An administrative-division sense is recorded, but its date and connection to examination or educational meanings are unclear.

limitations.text: Recorded meanings include assessment, taxation, teaching or study, and administrative division, but their full chronology and semantic connections are not established.
The exact first occurrence of 課 and the dates of lesson/course and administrative-division meanings remain unresolved.
